title: How to Use IB Mandarin B Exam Papers
summary: IB Mandarin B exam papers work best when you time each attempt, apply the markscheme, log errors, and revisit weak skills before the final exam.
body_markdown:
The value of an IB Mandarin B exam paper is not in completing it. The value is in discovering, with enough time to respond, exactly where marks are being lost.


In the final weeks, use each paper as part of a four-step cycle: complete a timed attempt, mark it strictly, record every meaningful error, then practise the weakest skill before trying another paper. That process turns a score into a revision plan.


A student who simply completes five papers may repeat the same mistakes five times. A student who studies two papers carefully can uncover recurring problems with text types, listening detail, vocabulary and question interpretation. Improvement comes from the review, not the volume.


### The final-weeks checklist


For every exam paper you attempt:


- Recreate the correct time limit and exam conditions.
- Keep notes, dictionaries and translation tools closed.
- Complete listening, reading and writing under realistic conditions.
- Mark receptive answers with the IB Mandarin B markscheme.
- Review writing against the published assessment criteria.
- Log the cause of every lost mark.
- Revisit the weakest theme, text type or language skill.
- Complete a short targeted drill within 24-48 hours.
- Return to the same weakness several days later.


This works because it separates performance from learning. The timed attempt shows what you can currently do. The review determines what you will do differently next time.


### Begin with a timed diagnostic attempt


Imagine a student with three weeks remaining. They feel reasonably comfortable reading Mandarin, less secure when listening, and uncertain about formal writing. Instead of revising everything equally, they sit one complete paper under timed conditions.


That first score is not a verdict. It is a map.


IB Language B external assessment includes Paper 1 for writing and Paper 2 for receptive skills, divided into listening and reading. The[IB Language B paper format guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/a-comprehensive-guide-to-the-ib-language-b-paper-format) explains how those components fit together. Students should confirm the timing and instructions for their own level and examination session before starting.


During the diagnostic attempt, reproduce the conditions that affect performance:


- Use only the materials permitted in the examination.
- Follow the official audio instructions and playback conditions.
- Do not pause to look up unfamiliar characters.
- Choose and complete a writing task without outside feedback.
- Stop when the allocated time ends, even if an answer is unfinished.


The discomfort is useful. It reveals whether the real problem is knowledge, speed, concentration or decision-making.


Two students looking at a revision calendar that has created another revision calendar


*An ambitious revision schedule discovers that planning can become another form of procrastination.*


### Use the IB Mandarin B markscheme actively


Self-marking should be slower than students expect. Checking whether an answer looks similar is not enough.


For listening and reading, compare each response with the accepted answer carefully. If an essential detail is absent, do not award yourself the mark simply because you understood the general idea. Strict marking creates a more useful diagnosis.


Beside each lost mark, write one reason:


- I did not know the word.
- I misread the question.
- I heard the sound but confused the meaning.
- I missed a negative, number or time expression.
- I copied incomplete evidence.
- I spent too long on an earlier item.


Writing requires a different review. The markscheme and criteria help you judge language, message and whether the response suits its purpose, audience and context. The[IB Chinese B Paper 1 writing guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-prepare-for-ib-chinese-b-paper-1-writing-exam-guide) is useful when prompt selection or text-type conventions are causing difficulty.


Do not ask only, “Is my Chinese correct?” Ask whether the response actually does the job. A grammatically strong answer can still lose marks if it ignores part of the prompt, adopts the wrong register or fails to use the conventions of the chosen text type.


### Build an error log that changes what you revise


An error log should be short enough to use. Record the paper section, the mistake, its cause and the next action.


For example, “Listening: missed the speaker’s change of opinion because I stopped taking notes after the first viewpoint. Action: practise contrast markers and listen for the final conclusion.” That is useful. “Need better listening” is not.


Group errors into four categories:


### Language gaps


These include unfamiliar vocabulary, inaccurate characters, weak sentence structures and confusion over connectors. Turn recurring vocabulary into[RevisionDojo Flashcards and Study Notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-free-features) , then test recognition in context rather than memorising isolated translations.


### Question-reading errors


A student may understand the passage but answer the wrong question. Circle instruction words and identify whether the item asks for a reason, example, opinion or supporting detail.


### Exam-technique errors


These include running out of time, writing too much for a low-value item or failing to return to a difficult question. Use the next timed session to test one specific adjustment.


### Theme and text-type weaknesses


The course is organised around identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organisation and sharing the planet. The[five prescribed themes in IB Chinese B](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-ib-chinese-b-connects-to-the-five-prescribed-themes) can help you organise vocabulary and examples without trying to predict an exact prompt.


If formal articles repeatedly cause trouble, review that format rather than writing another diary entry because it feels comfortable. The[guide to improving IB Chinese B writing](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-improve-writing-in-ib-chinese-b) can support this targeted practice.


### Revisit weak topics before attempting another full paper


A full paper identifies weaknesses, but it is often too broad to repair them. The next session should be narrower.


If the diagnostic attempt reveals weak listening for dates and quantities, complete a short drill focused on numbers, schedules and comparisons. If reading errors cluster around implied opinions, practise identifying tone and viewpoint. If writing lacks organisation, rewrite one response with a clearer opening, paragraph purpose and conclusion.

Build practice around the skill that failed, use AI Chat when an explanation remains unclear, and apply grading tools to understand how a response can improve. The wider platform also brings together Study Notes, Flashcards, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, a Coursework Library and Tutors, so the correction step does not become a search across unrelated resources.


The sequence matters:


1. Find the weakness under timed conditions.
2. Study the relevant rule, vocabulary or strategy.
3. Complete a small targeted set.
4. Return to a timed section and test whether the weakness remains.


That final step distinguishes recognition from improvement.


### Structure the remaining weeks


With three weeks left, a sensible pattern is one diagnostic paper, several targeted repair sessions, then another timed paper. During the second week, repeat the cycle while giving more attention to recurring errors. In the final week, reduce experimentation and focus on realistic timing, dependable structures and sleep.


Avoid completing a full paper every day. Mandarin performance depends on careful listening, reading precision and controlled writing, all of which require focused review. Constant simulation can produce fatigue without fixing the underlying problem.


Your final timed attempts should feel increasingly familiar. Use the[RevisionDojo Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/questionbank) for focused practice, then sit timed papers in Exam mode without interruptions. Review the result while the decisions you made are still fresh.


### Turn every attempt into the next decision


The final weeks often tempt students into measuring progress by pages completed. But marks rarely come from motion alone. They come from noticing that you misread comparison words, chose an unsuitable text type or repeatedly missed the speaker's final opinion, then correcting that pattern before exam day.


Treat every paper as evidence. Mark it honestly. Keep the error log specific. Revisit weak topics quickly. Then test them again under pressure.
